canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. The prevailing usage describes audio understanding as an ability to comprehend audio or auditory content. Most definitions keep the scope broad, covering audio signals or content such as speech, non-speech sounds, music, acoustic properties like pitch and timbre, and contextual sounds like environmental audio; one paper also frames it as mapping audio into meaningful linguistic representations. Papers agree on comprehension of audio as the core idea, but differ on scope: a smaller line narrows it to spoken dialogue systems' grasp of information beyond transcribed text, especially paralinguistic cues and environmental sounds, and another narrows it to environmental or other non-speech sound events.

Space of facets. Papers organize the construct by both content type and granularity. Some break it into speech, non-speech sounds, and music, while others emphasize fine-grained and coarse-grained analysis of signal properties such as frequency, amplitude, temporal patterns, pitch, timbre, and loudness, alongside contextual sounds. Papers use several nearby labels, including acoustic understanding, sound event understanding, and audio comprehension; one paper describes a sound event domain covering animals, the environment, and human activities, with tasks ranging from animal sound classification to emergency traffic detection and multi-channel sound event understanding.

Space of measurement. Papers connect the construct to 1 measurement instrument, MMAU, which is a benchmark, and to 1 behavioral indicator, Audio captioning. MMAU is used in complex audio QA tasks to evaluate understanding and reasoning capabilities, and one definition explicitly treats the construct as something inferred from performance across diverse audio-related tasks. No human evaluation, LLM-as-a-judge, or probe is linked to it.

Links. Beyond measurement, one paper claims a causal relationship from Semantic richness to Audio understanding, described through a semantic-rich tokenizer outperforming previous tokenizers on audio understanding and generation tasks. One paper also reports that Audio captioning is related to Audio understanding, treating audio captioning as one of the audio understanding tasks enabled by connecting audio encoders with large language models.

definitions.text: The ability of a spoken dialogue system to process and comprehend multi-modal information in audio beyond the transcribed text, such as paralinguistic cues and environmental sounds.
definitions.paper: VoxDialogue: Can Spoken Dialogue Systems Understand Information Beyond Words?

definitions.text: The ability to comprehend and process the fundamental properties of audio signals, including acoustic characteristics like pitch and timbre as well as contextual elements like environmental sounds.
definitions.paper: ADIFF: Explaining audio difference using natural language

definitions.text: The latent ability to comprehend audio content, including speech, non-speech sounds, and music, to interact effectively with the world.
definitions.paper: MMAU: A Massive Multi-Task Audio Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark

definitions.text: The latent ability to recognize and interpret environmental or non-speech sound sources and events.
definitions.paper: Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2: A Collaboratively Expanding Benchmark for Measuring the Capabilities of Spoken Language Models with 180 Tasks

definitions.text: The latent ability of a model to understand and interpret auditory content such as sound and music, inferred from performance across diverse audio-related tasks.
definitions.paper: MATS: An Audio Language Model under Text-only Supervision

relationships.paper: MATS: An Audio Language Model under Text-only Supervision
relationships.evidence: To further evaluate our model’s understanding and reasoning capabilities in complex audio QA tasks, we conducted experiments on AIR-Bench Chat (Yang et al., 2024) and MMAU (Sakshi et al., 2024) benchmarks. (Section 4.2.2)

relationships.paper: Enhancing Speech Large Language Models with Prompt-Aware Mixture of Audio Encoders
relationships.evidence: Connecting audio encoders with large language models (LLMs) allows the LLM to perform various audio understanding tasks, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) and audio captioning (AC). (Abstract)

definition_agreement.reason: Most papers define audio understanding as a model or system's ability to comprehend auditory content, but they differ in what part of that phenomenon they foreground: broad audio content including speech, music, and non-speech sounds, versus paralinguistic or acoustic properties, environmental sound events, or mapping audio into linguistic representations. These definitions still target the same kind of latent model ability, so they can be combined as different scopes or manifestations rather than conflicting constructs.
